### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, activities A19, A23, A26, A27, A28 occurred late in the trace (mean position around 0.69) and their most common successor was A34 (e.g., A19 → A34 in 100% of cases, A23 → A34 in 97.5%). In the later window, these activities occur early (mean position around 0.35) and their most common successor is A29 (e.g., A19 → A29 in 92%, A23 → A29 in 97%). [DIR001, DIR005, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, POS001, POS005, POS008, POS009, POS010]
- The main activities A20, A21, A22, A24, A25 moved from early (mean position ~0.39) to late (mean position ~0.64). Their successor set shifted from A29 (e.g., A20 → A29 17% before) to A34 (e.g., A20 → A34 18% after, A21 → A34 22% after). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS006, POS007, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR006, DIR007]
- The order between these two groups reversed: before, A20, A21, A22, A24, A25 preceded A29 and the early group; after, the early group precedes A29 and the main group. For example, A20 before A29 in 98.5% of traces before, but A29 before A20 in 98% after; similar reversals for A21, A22, A24, A25 with A29, and for pairs with A27, A28, A23. [REL004, REL009, REL014, REL021, REL025, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL023, REL024, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030]
- A33 and A44 also swapped their successor sets: A33 before led to the early group (A26, A19, A23, A28, A27), after to the main group (A24, A22, A25, A20, A21); A44 before led to the main group, after to the early group. [DIR011, DIR012]
- The co-occurrence of A34 with the early group dropped sharply (e.g., A27–A34 from 46 traces to 1, A28–A34 from 45 to 1), while co-occurrence of A34 with the main group rose (A20–A34 from 1 to 191, A21–A34 from 1 to 198). [LAG004, LAG005, LAG001, LAG002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a reversal of the order between two groups of activities. In the earlier window, the main activities (A20, A21, A22, A24, A25) occurred early, followed by A29, then the early-group activities (A19, A23, A26, A27, A28) late, with A34 as a successor of the early group. In the later window, the early-group activities occur first, followed by A29, then the main activities, with A34 now a successor of the main group. This is directly shown by position shifts (POS), successor changes (DIR), order reversals in co-occurring pairs (REL), and lag changes (LAG). The number of qualifying items (66) far exceeds the 0.88 expected by chance, and the items are consistent across indicators. A competing explanation of random sampling variation is ruled out by the screening comparison. A limitation is that the exact process structure (e.g., whether A34 and A29 are single activities or gateways) is not fully specified, but the behavioural reversal is clear.

Other differences: A33 and A44 also swapped their positions relative to the two groups, consistent with the same reversal. No time or resource changes were reported.
